item.title: Permeable by design
item.description:
Representative article figure (not a graphical abstract)

Nature Reviews Chemistry, Published online: 24 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41570-026-00871-2

Mycobacterial drug discovery is held back by the challenge of limited compound penetration across the mycomembrane. An experimentally enabled machine-learning approach identifies permeability-promoting molecular features that could help guide medicinal chemistry toward more permeable antibacterial candidates.

item.title: Watching ice nucleation in real-time
item.description:
Representative article figure (not a graphical abstract)

Nature Reviews Chemistry, Published online: 20 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41570-026-00870-3

Devendra Pal explains how their custom-made ice nucleation chamber works, yielding data on nucleation itself as well as particle sizes, phases, and morphologies in an effort to understand cloud formation and its impact on atmospheric chemistry.

item.title: An expert in creating complex structures
item.description:

Nature Reviews Chemistry, Published online: 20 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41570-026-00869-w

Ahead of her 65th birthday, Margaret Brimble, Distinguished Professor and Director of Medicinal Chemistry at the University of Auckland, discussed her life in science.

item.title: Molten salt electrochemistry for next-generation batteries
item.description:
Representative article figure (not a graphical abstract)

Nature Reviews Chemistry, Published online: 20 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41570-026-00866-z

This Review discusses molten salt electrochemistry for energy storage systems, covering electrolyte chemistry, charge storage, cell configurations and materials innovations, and points to future opportunities in cathode design, ion-selective membranes and advanced molten salt systems.

item.title: Subcellular photochemistry for precision spatial protein targeting
item.description:
Representative article figure (not a graphical abstract)

Nature Reviews Chemistry, Published online: 20 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41570-026-00864-1

Conventional drug design lacks the spatial control needed for the selective targeting of mislocalized proteins, a pervasive phenomenon with diseases. This Perspective discusses how subcellular photochemistry combined with a prodrug approach can target those conserved proteins precisely.

item.title: Targeting soluble misfolded oligomers in anti-amyloid research
item.description:
Representative article figure (not a graphical abstract)

Nature Reviews Chemistry, Published online: 20 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41570-026-00867-y

This Review surveys emerging chemical and biophysical tools for detection, characterization and intervention of soluble misfolded oligomers. These small oligomers are considered the main disease-causing species for amyloid diseases. Targeting these oligomers is highlighted as a promising research direction.

item.title: Atmospheric chemistry of volatile methyl siloxanes
item.description:
Representative article figure (not a graphical abstract)

Nature Reviews Chemistry, Published online: 17 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41570-026-00862-3

Volatile methyl siloxanes are synthetic compounds that readily partition to the atmosphere and have been a focus of policy debates. This Review discusses advances in understanding the atmospheric chemistry, lifetimes and abundancies of these compounds and their oxidation products.

item.title: The automated red pen
item.description:
Representative article figure (not a graphical abstract)

Nature Reviews Chemistry, Published online: 10 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41570-026-00868-x

Large language models can grade a stack of chemistry assignments before the kettle has boiled. Whether we should let them depends less on speed than on purpose. Before an AI marker influences grades, it should be validated like an analytical method, with defined limits, quality control and a route to appeal.
